n: Outside Eden, Adam farmed the land and cared for the animals, earning his bread by hard work as God said. Eve labored alongside him—they were partners from the start.

f.w: Eve, also, his wife, did labor with him
f.g: A Moses addition emphasizing partnership; not in Genesis.

n: Adam and Eve had sons and daughters, who began to fill the earth. Genesis mentions only Cain, Abel, and Seth at first; Moses shows a larger family existed.

f.g: “Knew” is a biblical idiom for marital intimacy.

f.w: she bare unto him sons and daughters

n: Their children paired off, spread out, farmed, kept flocks, and had families of their own.

f.g: Pair off as couples.

n: Adam and Eve prayed together and heard the Lord’s voice from the direction of Eden, though they couldn’t see him—they were now shut out of his presence. Even fallen, they still sought God.

f.w: called upon the name of the Lord

n: God commanded them to worship him and offer the firstborn of their flocks as sacrifices. Adam obeyed.

f.g: The firstborn animals—the best, given first.

n: After “many days,” an angel asked Adam why he offered sacrifices. Adam answered, “I know not, save the Lord commanded me”—a model of faithful obedience before full understanding.

f.w: I know not, save the Lord commanded me

n: The angel explains: the sacrifice is a likeness of the coming sacrifice of the Only Begotten. From the beginning, animal sacrifice pointed to Christ.

f.w: a similitude of the sacrifice of the Only Begotten

n: Adam is to do everything in the Son’s name and to repent and pray in his name forever.

f.w: in the name of the Son

n: The Holy Ghost fell on Adam and testified of Christ: as Adam fell, he and all who are willing can be redeemed.

f.w: as thou hast fallen thou mayest be redeemed

f.g: Redemption is offered to all but requires willingness.

n: Adam, filled with the Spirit, prophesied and blessed God: because of the transgression his eyes are opened, he will have joy in this life, and in the flesh he will see God again.

f.w: in this life I shall have joy
again in the flesh I shall see God

n: Eve’s great insight: without the transgression they would never have had children, known good and evil, or experienced redemption and eternal life. Latter-day Saints honor Eve’s wisdom and courage.

f.w: Were it not for our transgression we never should have had seed

n: They praised God and taught everything to their children—the first gospel teachers in a family.

f.w: made all things known unto their sons and their daughters

n: Satan came claiming to be a son of God too and told them not to believe. Many children chose Satan over God, and people became “carnal, sensual, and devilish”—driven by appetite and evil.

f.w: I am also a son of God
f.g: Satan again attacks identity, as he did with Moses (Moses 1:12-19).

n: God called people everywhere to repent through the Holy Ghost.

f.w: called upon men by the Holy Ghost everywhere

n: Those who believed in the Son and repented would be saved; those who didn’t would be condemned—a firm decree.

f.w: as many as believed in the Son

n: Adam and Eve kept praying. Eve bore Cain and hoped he would follow God, but Cain refused: “Who is the Lord that I should know him?”—echoing Pharaoh’s defiance.

f.w: I have gotten a man from the Lord
Who is the Lord that I should know him?

n: Then Abel was born, and he obeyed the Lord. Abel kept sheep; Cain farmed.

f.w: Abel hearkened unto the voice of the Lord

n: Cain loved Satan more than God, and Satan told him to make an offering. His worship was prompted by the wrong source.

f.w: Cain loved Satan more than God

n: Cain brought produce from his fields as an offering.
Abel brought the firstborn of his flock and the best parts. The Lord accepted Abel’s offering—given in faith as commanded.

f.w: the firstlings of his flock, and of the fat thereof

n: The Lord did not accept Cain’s offering. Satan was pleased; Cain was furious, and his face fell.

f.g: Very angry.
His expression darkened in anger or sullenness.

n: God gently asks Cain why he is angry—an invitation to reflect.
If Cain does well, he will be accepted. Otherwise sin waits at the door, and Satan wants him. Cain could still choose.

f.g: Pictured as a crouching animal waiting to pounce.

n: Cain would become “the father of his lies” and be called Perdition—he too existed before the world. A sobering warning about where his path leads.

f.g: Ruin, loss; a name also given to Satan.

f.w: thou wast also before the world

n: These evils would be traced back to Cain because he rejected God’s greater counsel—unless he repented. Even here, repentance is offered.
Cain refused to listen to God or to his righteous brother Abel.
Adam and Eve mourned over Cain and their other wayward children—parents’ grief over choices they cannot control.
Cain married one of his nieces, and they loved Satan more than God.

f.g: In the earliest generations, marriage within the family was necessary.

n: Satan has Cain swear a secret oath on his life, and his followers too, to keep it hidden, especially from Adam. In return Satan promises to deliver Abel into his hands.

f.w: Swear unto me by thy throat
f.g: An oath sealed with a death penalty for breaking it.

n: Satan swore to do as Cain wished. It was all done in secret—the origin of secret combinations.

f.w: all these things were done in secret

n: Cain called himself “Mahan,” master of this secret—killing for gain—and gloried in his wickedness.

f.g: The meaning of Mahan is uncertain; it may relate to “mind” or “destroyer.”

f.w: that I may murder and get gain

n: In the field, Cain spoke with Abel and then rose up and killed him—the first murder.
Cain boasted, “I am free”—now his brother’s flocks were his. Sin promises freedom but brings bondage.

f.g: A tragic irony; Cain becomes a fugitive.

n: God asks where Abel is. Cain lies and retorts, “Am I my brother’s keeper?” The scriptures answer yes—we are responsible for one another.
Abel’s blood cries out to God from the ground. Injustice does not go unseen.

f.w: The voice of thy brother's blood cries unto me

n: Cain is cursed from the earth that received Abel’s blood.
The ground will no longer yield its strength to him; he will be a restless wanderer.

f.g: A homeless wanderer.

n: Cain blames Satan and jealousy over the offering, and complains his punishment is too great—but shows no real repentance.

f.w: my punishment is greater than I can bear

n: Cain fears being cut off from God and killed by others because of his sins.

f.w: from thy face shall I be hid

n: God promises sevenfold vengeance on anyone who kills Cain and gives him a mark of protection. Scripture does not say what the mark was; the Church disavows past theories linking it to race.

f.g: Seven times over; complete retribution.

n: Shut out from God’s presence, Cain lived with his wife and followers in Nod, east of Eden.

f.g: Nod means “wandering.”

n: Cain had a son named Enoch (not the prophet Enoch) and built a city named after him.
Cain’s line continues: Enoch, Irad, Mahujael, Methusael, and Lamech.

f.g: This Lamech is not Noah’s father, who descended from Seth.

n: Lamech married two wives, Adah and Zillah—the first recorded plural marriage.
Adah’s sons founded tent-dwelling herding and music. Culture and skill spread even in a wicked line.

f.g: Stringed instruments and pipes or flutes.

n: Zillah’s son Tubal Cain became the first metalworker; his sister was Naamah.

f.g: A skilled craftsman.

n: Lamech boasts to his wives that he has killed a man who wounded him.

f.w: I have slain a man to my wounding

n: If Cain is avenged sevenfold, Lamech claims seventy-sevenfold—escalating vengeance. Jesus later reversed this with “seventy times seven” forgiveness.
Moses explains: Lamech had made Satan’s covenant like Cain and become Master Mahan. Irad, Cain’s grandson, began revealing the secret.
So Lamech killed Irad—not for gain like Cain, but to protect the oath.

f.g: To enforce secrecy.

n: From Cain’s days there was a secret combination; its works were done in darkness, and members knew each other.
God cursed Lamech and all who covenanted with Satan. Their abominations spread among men.

f.g: God withdrew his presence and help.

n: Lamech had told his wives the secret, and they rebelled and spread it abroad—women here help expose the evil.

f.g: A Moses addition; the wives refused complicity.

n: Lamech was despised and cast out, hiding for fear of death.

f.g: Expelled from society.

n: So works of darkness began to dominate humanity.
God cursed the earth severely and was angry with the wicked.

f.g: Sore = severe.

n: They refused to listen or believe in the Only Begotten, who would come in “the meridian of time,” prepared before the world.

f.g: The high point or middle of history—the time of Christ’s mortal life.

f.w: prepared from before the foundation of the world

n: A key Restoration teaching: the gospel of Jesus Christ was preached from the very beginning—by angels, God’s voice, and the Holy Ghost.

f.w: the Gospel began to be preached, from the beginning

n: All was confirmed to Adam by a holy ordinance, and a decree went out that the gospel would remain in the world until the end.

f.g: Moses 6:64-66 describes Adam’s baptism.
